body.prose:
Where the reader looks is the page's address, the truth of it: the expression said as text, as `?look=Group+by(Not(Children+of(Everything)),:auto)`, in a syntax made for an address, using only what an address carries as it is: titles, parentheses and commas, a holon after @ by the shortest end of its id no other holon's id ends with, words after :, a space as +; and the component it is looked at with, where one was chosen. The text is said and read by a pair of pure functions, the syntax, so it can change without anything that holds expressions changing. The root mount is offered the place the address names; it holds only what is the reader's, the component it calls and what it offers, their favorites and settings. To look somewhere else is a new address, a step in the browser's own history; back and forward are only the address changing, and nothing is written to go back, for commits are a line and are never undone. What the reader has looked at is kept in the field as their history, a holon in the home that each move adds a visit to, when and what, said as text, so a visit points at nothing that can be gone; going back adds none. This is where the browser and the field meet, an integration, kept in the interface until glass runs programs. A reader that is not the root, as one laid over another place, is a mount like any other, and needs no address. A mount found within what another draws, as the entry pressed in a list, is shown, not run: what it is called, the component it calls, and what it gives, pressed to look there; and a mount never moves to itself.

A press does not need catching from above. Every slot says where it is: its element carries the holons it reads as its location, and a link in prose carries the one it mentions. A press rises through the page from where it landed, past those locations, to whatever holds them and cares. The mount component cares, where it may write its mount: a press inside it gives the innermost location it passed, and the mount gives that instead, drawn again by the component the entry calls, the reader. The brief that was pressed never knows it was read; a mount that may not be written lets a press rise on.

Where one is looking is said above it by the search, the first of the reader's two mounts, given what the second draws. An expression is said by its parts, each a function and what it is given, as a field and a value: Type: Brief, Children of: The plan, Text: reader, Not: Store: home, Group by: auto, each a chip pressed to change it, or, given holons, to add one or take one out, and let go with its ×; a holon by what it is, each type a way to its kind, and what it is called, let go for everything. Every function the field holds is a brick, glass's own and one's own alike, offered by its title; at the top, the parts standing side by side are And and no part at all is Everything, while within a brick, And and Everything are taken like any other. Typing finds the brick, Enter takes it, and what it takes is chosen in turn: a set among what is in view, the types and parents of what one is looking at, each with how many it holds, a store among the stores in view, or among the holons whose title says what is typed, or built of another brick taken within it; words as they are typed; an axis to group by. Once all it takes is given, it stands as one more part beside the others, under And; a part given holons is given another by pressing it and choosing a second, as Type: Brief or Component, and Or builds an either of any parts; Open goes to one holon. Typed with no brick taken, the words find the values in view as well, as Type: Brief. Backspace lets go of the brick taken last, then of the last part; Escape lets go of what was typed, then of what was taken; in a menu, it closes the menu. Typed, the words find first the holons whose title begins with them, so a holon is found by its name. Before anything is typed it offers the favorites and the bricks, and asks nothing. Each thing it offers that leads somewhere is a press that says where, and rises to the mount like any other: a place, a place drawn by a component, an expression, what the mount offers, or an expression to keep. Nothing is born as one moves: the mount holds the expression it gives.

The secondary press rises the same way, and the mount lays the same search where it landed, given the place pressed, the component it is drawn by, and the settings its slot gave, so what can be done there is found as anything is. The place was drawn, not held, so the menu changes nothing of it: its parts are said from here, not changed or let go, and what is built from them is looked at instead. It offers to look there, a holon or a way of looking alike; to look there with each other component that takes it, for that one look; to set what that component takes and nothing gave it, as cards for a list or for a grouping's collections, which the mount then offers to all it draws; a face stands in what holds it, as an item in a list, so its settings to set are its own and its holder's; to keep a way of looking on the favorites, born then as a function of one's own that takes nothing and gives it, which opens in the search as what it gives, so its parts can be seen and changed, or to place a holon there or take it off. The search is what the mount is offered as its search, and the favorites what it offers, so both are the reader's to change, as data; a favorite no longer in the field is let go of as the mount is next written.

```ts
holon The root : Mount {          // the reader's own, in the home
  component: ref(Reader)
  offer: {
    search:    ref(Search)                      // what its menu is drawn by
    favorites: [ ref(Briefs of the day) ]       // a function of one's own, kept
    cards:     true                             // a list's setting, offered to all it draws
  }
}
```

*The author's, 2026-11-03: navigation needs a kind of history and is based on locations; the reader needs a way to see the actual location you are looking at and to be able to update it, for a face of it is not that helpful, and not by presets or raw text, but ontologically, naturally; the root holds the expression for what you are seeing, and changing it from the context menu's WYSIWYG is fine; the context menu has actual actions, made available by type matching; the history stack and the URL as an integration. Bubbling the session's proposal, which the author was open to; catching every press at the root was OpenLight's answer, not taken for granted. Programs, once they run, are where more of the menu's actions will come from. The address the author's, the day after: it still has to be real history; commits you can't reverse, so the browser's history is not walked by writing old versions again; the URL as the source of truth, either the expression broken apart in it or a history element; a parser is just a function, so the syntax can change later; a URL-adapted language, as URL-pragmatic as possible; ids need not be that big in an address. Functions are called by their titles until holons carry names of their own, as [the relations](ref:01M6M9PESEPYSZBYWQVD709ACJ) tell. The search the author's, the same evening: expressions are ontology, every part has meaning; the formula said at the top, visualized and editable, a smart search across expressions, briefs and holons, narrowing by type to build an intersection, a made expression found by its name; favorites the reader looks for; a list's cards set by right-clicking it; and the search one common component, the context menu a very similar thing, its input everything or already narrowed. A setting as an offer the author's correction of the session's mount settings. Or as a join of the next part to the last let go the same night, as the author found it confusing; Or is built as any brick is. The bricks the author's, later that evening: say type, then Enter, and choose; all the Lego bricks, to add to an intersection and build an expression in place, not a plethora to search and select from. Plain words, a field and its value, and a mature feature set, the author's, the same night: what it is, by type, store rather than kept in. Only settings that are true or false are offered to set so far; a node-based builder for complex expressions is not built.*
body.title: Moving is a new address
